title: Inverse image of an inverse tower with compatible local bases
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with finite limits, whose objects and morphisms are small in one universe, and take sheaves of sets, abelian groups, rings and modules in a larger universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite limits and coverings, and write $f^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for its geometric inverse image [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. Let $(R_n,\rho_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an inverse tower of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. For each $n$ let $M_n$ be an $R_n$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with additive transition $t_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$ satisfying $t_n(a m)=\rho_n(a)t_n(m)$. Put $R=\varprojlim_n R_n$ and $M=\varprojlim_n M_n$, with sectionwise ring and module operations [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Suppose the canonical projection-induced ring map
$$\kappa:f^{-1}R\longrightarrow\varprojlim_n f^{-1}R_n$$
is an isomorphism. Suppose there is a covering $\{V_i\to1_{\mathcal C}\}$ and, for every $i,n$, an $R_n|_{V_i}$-linear isomorphism $b_{i,n}:R_n|_{V_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n|_{V_i}$, such that $t_n b_{i,n+1}=b_{i,n}\rho_n$ after restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Then the canonical projection-induced comparison
$$\theta:f^{-1}M\longrightarrow\varprojlim_n f^{-1}M_n$$
is an isomorphism, linear over $\kappa$ when the right hand side has its coordinatewise $\varprojlim_n f^{-1}R_n$-action. The maps $b_{i,n}$ induce $R|_{V_i}\cong M|_{V_i}$, and on $\mathcal D/u(V_i)$ these identifications identify $\theta$ with the restriction of $\kappa$. The comparison is natural for homomorphisms of ring towers and compatible semilinear morphisms of module towers; it does not depend on the chosen covering or bases.

proof.text: For each index $i$, the compatible maps $b_{i,n}$ form an isomorphism of inverse systems on the localized site $\mathcal C/V_i$: their transition compatibility is exactly $t_n b_{i,n+1}=b_{i,n}\rho_n$. The sectionwise description of inverse limits therefore gives an isomorphism $b_i:R|_{V_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}M|_{V_i}$, with inverse induced by the inverses $b_{i,n}^{-1}$. It is $R|_{V_i}$-linear because the action on the limit is coordinatewise and each $b_{i,n}$ is $R_n|_{V_i}$-linear.

proof.text: Establish continuity directly from the covering-pullback axiom and preservation of finite limits. Mathlib left Kan extension and sheafification preserve finite limits, using AB5 at the smaller site universe. Apply lem-pur-unit-normalized-slice-inverse-image to obtain a natural local inverse-image functor, a natural unit family, and the comparison with global inverse image followed by restriction. Conjugating the image of each local basis by this comparison gives the local inverse-image basis, with the required actual-unit equation.

source.place: Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism; the inverse-image comparison after localization.

proof.text: Restriction preserves limits because it is precomposition and the sheaf inclusion creates limits. Assemble the transported level bases as a natural isomorphism of towers; the limits and preservation comparisons give B double-prime. Naturality of the slice comparison and the original projection equations give the local comparison square by joint monicity of the restricted limit projections. Separately, semilinearity makes level scalar actions a natural transformation from the product tower. Their limit gives the coordinatewise action. Transport it through the inverse of the binary-product comparison; naturality of that comparison and the limit projections prove all scalar equations and linearity.

source.place: Integral twist paragraph: on each compatible-generator chart the module comparison is identified with the coefficient-ring comparison.

proof.text: The image under U of the given terminal-object cover is covering. On each image slice the local comparison square expresses the module comparison as the conjugate of the assumed invertible ring comparison. Its components are therefore bijective on every object admitting a map to this image chart. Pull back the generated covering sieve along the unique map of any object to U(1). On every arrow of that covering sieve a chartwise bijection proves local injectivity and local surjectivity. Apply the sheaf local-bijection criterion to conclude that the global comparison is invertible.

source.place: Integral twist paragraph: descend the chartwise identification by the sheaf criterion on the compatible-generator cover.

proof.text: The construction uses only canonical projection maps and the given tower morphisms. Hence it is natural for morphisms of ring towers and compatible semilinear morphisms of module towers. The local identification with $\kappa$ is forced by the commuting projection squares, so changing the covering or the chosen compatible bases changes only the intermediate local witnesses, not $\theta$ or its inverse; the comparison is therefore independent of those choices.

source.place: Integral twist paragraph: naturality and independence of the chosen compatible local bases.

split_report.summary: Checked the imported local-basis argument against the blueprint and Stacks Tag 03CF. The compatible bases give an inverse-limit isomorphism on each chosen chart; slice-site localization identifies the pullback restriction with the localized inverse image, so the comparison is locally the assumed ring comparison. Cover stability and the sheaf local-isomorphism criterion globalize it, while the projection-based construction gives linearity, naturality, and independence of choices. No auxiliary node was needed because all non-elementary ingredients were already recorded in the DAG.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the integral twist paragraph: (1) compatible local bases induce the limit-ring/module identification; (2) localization transports it across inverse image; (3) the comparison is locally the coefficient comparison; (4) sheaf descent gives the global isomorphism; (5) canonical projections give naturality and choice independence.
